question: How does BSP actually buy companies?
html:
BSP buys theme-first. It studies a sector in advance, then wins a banked process for an anchor acquisition, either from another sponsor (larger checks) or from founders taking first institutional capital (smaller checks). This pattern is reverse-engineered from public evidence, not BSP's internal screening criteria (BSP acquisition methodology).

Thesis before target

  • Deal releases present each company as the output of a sector thesis. RJ David spent "over a year" in electrical services before CET, and Adam Glucksman watched accounting before Smith + Howard (BSP acquisition methodology).
  • Since 2024 the filter has narrowed to essential services. Punctual Pros, Frontline and CET are all non-discretionary. Fair Harbor remains the only discretionary consumer bet (BSP acquisition methodology).

Two seller types

Anchor dealDateSellerCEO outcome
Thomas ScientificJan 27, 2022CarlyleReplaced (Simmons to Haas)
Fair HarborMar 23, 2022FoundersFounder stays
Smith + HowardNov 15, 2022PartnersNot stated
BPIApr 27, 2023SvobodaBleeker continues
Punctual ProsApr 3, 2024FoundersMatt Buckwalter stays
FrontlineDec 11, 2024BVReplaced (Naidoo to Britt)
CETFeb 2025Founder/managementJohn Duquette Jr. stays

Sources: BSP acquisition methodology; BSP firm profile.

  • In secondaries the outgoing sponsor often rolls a minority stake (Svoboda at BPI, BV at Frontline).
  • Inherited CEOs are replaced at about 13-15 months. Founder CEOs stay.

Banked, repeat advisers

  • Six of seven anchor deals had a named sell-side adviser. Punctual Pros went to "eight finalists."
  • Berenson advised BSP on Thomas, BPI, Frontline and CET. Harris Williams advised on Punctual Pros and Frontline. Morrison Cohen or Greenberg Traurig was counsel on every deal (BSP acquisition methodology).
  • Structures vary. Smith + Howard used an alternative practice structure. Thomas used an Apollo/MidCap unitranche. Fair Harbor shows no debt on public record.

Capital constraints

  • The main fund reports $335M sold (Form D). A $136.95M Frontline deal vehicle suggests heavy use of co-invest (BSP firm profile). The $50-250M check range is unverified.
  • Rivals run $0.9-2.1B flagships, so BSP leans on co-invest and operating credibility (Private-equity landscape).

Add-ons follow

  • BSP states 23 add-ons, and 21 are identified by name. Fair Harbor and Frontline have none (BSP acquisition methodology).
  • For Punctual Pros, the landscape points to proprietary outreach to sub-$3M EBITDA shops instead of auctions (est., Private-equity landscape).

Gaps

  • Entry multiples, leverage at close and BSP's equity share per deal are not in the context. Closing statements or lender filings would answer them.

Next actions

  • Confirm the two unnamed add-ons (one Punctual Pros, one Smith + Howard) to close the 23-versus-21 gap.
  • Pull entry multiples and leverage for each anchor deal to test the size-band inference.
  • Build a proprietary sourcing list for Frontline legal-IT and billing add-ons before generalist MSP consolidators move in.
  • Track the CEO succession pattern against current secondary-deal hold periods.
